title: Dead-letter queues and poison messages

kcs.statement: A poison message fails processing every time, so under at-least-once delivery it is redelivered forever, wasting consumer capacity and, in an ordered queue or partition, blocking everything behind it.
After a maximum number of delivery attempts the message is moved to a dead-letter queue, which needs alerting and a redrive path so engineers can inspect, fix and replay the messages.

problem_ideas: A malformed JSON message is at the head of a FIFO queue: describe the system's behaviour with and without a DLQ
Choose max delivery attempts for a payment-webhook consumer vs a thumbnail generator and justify
DLQ receives 50 messages/min after a deploy: what's your runbook?
Distinguish transient failures (database timeout) from permanent ones (schema mismatch): which should hit the DLQ fast?
After fixing a bug you redrive 10,000 DLQ messages: what must the consumer guarantee?
In an event stream partition, how does one poison event stall a whole partition?
